subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Anti-Corruption in Procurement
description: A quick, practical guide to Anti-Corruption in Procurement.

hook.text: A buyer steers a $10 million contract to a friend's company. The kickback was $200,000. Both go to prison.

buildup.text: Procurement fraud—kickbacks, bid rigging, and bribery—costs organizations billions globally each year.

discovery.text: Segregation of duties, approval thresholds, and audit trails are key controls against corruption.

twist.text: Laws like the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act make companies liable even if bribery happens overseas.

climax.text: Siemens paid $1.6 billion in fines for procurement bribery. The cost of corruption always exceeds the gain.

punchline.text: Corruption in procurement is a crime with a paper trail.

quiz.question: What is a key control against procurement fraud?
options: Segregation of duties and audit trails
